entity-ungrouped-transition-morphscene-entity-transitions0.75 of 0.75 (major)passFor steps with different group keys, Stage keys the wrapper on groupKey ?? id inside AnimatePresence (default sync mode). entity-newcomer-after-settlescene-entity-transitions0.75 of 0.75 (major)passNewcomer entry is delayed by ENTER_DELAY, which equals the continuing layout duration LAYOUT_T (0.5s). The delay is applied only to the opacity entry, not to layout motion. Every entity the sample introduces goes through this path. In Entity, `initial={appear ? {opacity:0} : undefined}` and `animate={appear ? {opacity:1, transition:{delay: ENTER_DELAY, duration: ENTER_T, ease: EASE}} : undefined}` put the delay on the opacity animation alone. Layout motion uses the separate `transition={{ layout: { duration: LAYOUT_T, ease: EASE } }}` with no delay. A continuing entity therefore starts moving immediately, over 0.5s. A newcomer stays at opacity 0 for 0.5s and then fades in, so its visible entry starts at or after the moment the layout move ends. Because opacity is only initialised on mount, an entity that stays mounted under the same key is not re-faded. SampleScene renders every entity through `renderEntity`, which calls Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, Label, SymbolChip and Box. The Arrow case passes `appear` explicitly. The other cases spread `common = { id, className, appear: true, ...box }`. Arrow spreads `...props` into Entity, and Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame and Emphasis each render `&lt;Entity kind=... {...props}/&gt;` with `appear` unchanged. So all six entity kinds in the sample get the delayed entry, and none appears without entry motion. The `parts` spans in a Box are unidentified wrappers, not entities. SceneLayer wraps the children in `AnimatePresence initial={false}`, which only skips animation for the first render. Entities added on later steps still animate in. The unit test in nodes.test.tsx checks newcomer opacity &#39;0&#39; against the continuing entity&#39;s &#39;&#39;, that ENTER_DELAY &gt;= LAYOUT_T, that opacity is still 0 at 40% of the delay, and that it reaches 1 later. That test uses `Appear`, which the sample does not use. review_._all-reviewers (1) - skills/presentation/scripts/presentation-scaffold.mjs:232 fill() passes user-controlled `values.title` as the replacement string to String.replaceAll. Replacement strings interpret `$&`, `$'`, `` $` `` and `$$`. Trace: `add --title \"Save $$$\"` (or a title containing `$'`) goes through `JSON.stringify` into `__TITLE_JSON__`, then into `replaceAll`. `$$` collapses to `$`, and `$'` inserts the rest of the template. Talk.tsx and style.css are silently corrupted, or fail to compile, with no error. Separately, the title is substituted before `__NAME__`/`__SLUG__`, so a title containing `__NAME__` is rewritten by the later replacements. Not confirmed by running it.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - scripts/lib/preview.mjs:29 readRegistry parses the registry with a regex `title:\\s*(['\"])(.*?)\\3`. addPresentation writes titles with JSON.stringify, so a title containing a double quote is written as `\\\"`. The lazy match stops at the escaped quote and returns a truncated title. A title with a backslash is returned still escaped. `inspect`'s 'unknown presentation' listing therefore shows wrong titles. The title mismatch is cosmetic. The deeper risk is that this regex-based registry parser silently drops entries that don't match the exact `slug` then `title` ordering, for example a hand-edited entry with `title` first. Verify would then skip that presentation and still print PASS.\n ✓ Fixed: review_._all-reviewers (1) - skills/presentation/scripts/presentation-scaffold.mjs:217 The result of `npx playwright install chromium` is reduced to `browserInstalled = status === 0`, and nothing is logged or raised if it fails. The scaffold then reports success, and the user only finds out when `npm run verify` fails later with a launch error. review_._all-reviewers (1) - skills/presentation/scripts/presentation-scaffold.mjs:185 Precondition: a parent package.json lists the target through a workspace pattern that `match` doesn't handle. Examples are a mid-path wildcard like `apps/*/web`, a bare `*`, a brace pattern, or a pattern with a `!` negation. Trace: `match` only handles a trailing `/**`, a trailing `/*`, or an exact string, so any other pattern falls through to `clean === rel` and returns false. A non-string entry makes `pattern.replace` throw, and the empty `catch` hides that. `isWorkspaceMember` then returns false and `installCommand` picks `ci` whenever the member has its own lockfile and no deps were added. Failure: `npm ci` fails for a real workspace member, because npm requires the root lockfile. That is the bug this change is meant to fix, and it comes back for these patterns. The failure message (`npm ci failed in ...`) gives no hint that workspace detection was the cause. The catch also treats a malformed manifest as 'not a workspace root' without saying so. Uncertain: how common these patterns are in this project's scaffold targets.\n\n━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━\nTotal: 1 fixed, 0 skipped, 0 failed after 2 iterations\nStatus: Identity: entities.ts defines the presentation-owned ID namespace (htp-*) and an EntitySpec for every entity, each carrying its ID member as id. Steps import these spec objects and build cumulative lists (02 spreads 01&#39;s entities, 03 spreads 02&#39;s, and so on through 09). A persisting entity is therefore the same spec with the same id at every later step. Scene.tsx renderEntity destructures id and forwards it as the id and React key to every kind. Box, Label, SymbolChip, Frame and Emphasis spread their props into Entity. Arrow passes id={id} explicitly. Entity.tsx sets motion.div layout and layoutId={id}, plus data-presentation-entity={id}. The persisting layoutId inside the shared LayoutGroup gives the kit&#39;s morph-in-place for same-identity entities. SceneLayer keys children by id inside AnimatePresence. Entities that disappear animate out, and entities that persist are not remounted. Stage.tsx computes key = step.groupKey ?? step.id and renders one keyed motion.div inside LayoutGroup and AnimatePresence. All nine steps give the same key, so the scene stays mounted and only the payload changes. Grouping is therefore proven. Identity is proven separately through the presentation-owned ID constants in entities.ts. Each EntitySpec carries id: ID.&lt;member&gt;. Steps build cumulative lists by spreading the previous step&#39;s entities array, so a persisting entity keeps the same spec and id. Scene.tsx renderEntity forwards id and key={id} to Arrow, Frame, Emphasis, Label, SymbolChip and Box. The kit nodes pass id to Entity, either through props or, for Arrow, explicitly. Entity.tsx sets layout, layoutId={id} and data-presentation-entity={id}. SceneLayer keys children by id inside AnimatePresence. None of these test files calls waitForTimeout, setTimeout or any other sleep, and none reads a value that returns immediately as if it had waited. The scripts they drive wait for the step with a polling page.waitForFunction on data-step-index, and for the first render with waitForSelector on data-step-count. The only fixed sleep in any test file is tests/unit/nodes.test.tsx:84. That file runs under the jsdom environment (vitest.config.ts), not a browser. The sleep is a deliberate negative check that the newcomer is still hidden before the entry delay. Arrival of the target state is then awaited with a polling waitFor. Judges A and B ruled pass on this basis, and the material bears them out. Judge C failed the criterion because verify.mjs calls page.waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS) and inspect uses page.waitForTimeout(options.settle). That reason does not decide the requirement. Those sleeps are in the verification tooling under test, not in the test files. In verify.mjs the sleep runs only after the polling waitForFunction has already confirmed data-step-index, so it does not replace the wait for the step. Inspect&#39;s --settle interval is a product feature, and inspect.test.ts lines 118-126 assert that feature (settledMs &gt;= settle); the test is not using a sleep in place of waiting for state. Judge C argued for fail because those scripts then call waitForTimeout(SETTLE_MS) or options.settle. That pause comes after the state wait, not instead of it. The step-index assertion is already satisfied by the polling waitForFunction. The inspect settle interval is a feature the tests exercise and assert on (inspect.test.ts:118-124). The guidance also lists longer fixed settle delays as validator noise. So C&#39;s reason does not show any browser test sleeping instead of waiting for state. dispute_checks{"demo-integration":[],"scene-kit":[],"presentation-skill":[{"id":"skill-failures-fixed-before-success","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The contradiction does not hold. SKILL.md §4 tells the agent to run build, verify and inspect and to &quot;fix everything that fails; never report success on broken output&quot;. Each kind of finding the auditor lists comes with a required fix: &quot;fix accidental text or chrome collisions, give the active progress/TOC entry a visibly distinct style, and style the attribution link so it is legible&quot;. Only overlaps that are genuinely intentional and readable may be marked with allowOverlap, and then the helper must be rerun. The quality bar also requires that every presentation &quot;passes the visual check&quot;. So the instructions do not let a collision, active-chrome problem or attribution problem be reported instead of fixed. The sentence &quot;report any that remain, with the reason&quot; covers heuristic WARN output that is still there after the required fix-and-rerun pass. inspect-presentation.mjs itself calls these warnings advisory, and they are not failures of the build, render or composition check. The review guidance says that fixing visual composition findings and re-inspecting satisfies the visual check. It also says the criterion must not fail for a failure mode of a check tool, and that a field in the completion report (§5&#39;s &quot;remaining advisory warnings&quot;) does not permit completing with a failing check. Nothing in the material lets the skill complete while a build, render or visual composition check is failing.","evidence":["SKILL.md §4: &quot;Run, from &lt;target&gt;, and fix everything that fails; never report success on broken output&quot;","SKILL.md §4: &quot;fix accidental text or chrome collisions, give the active progress/TOC entry a visibly distinct style, and style the attribution link so it is legible. Mark only genuinely intentio…","SKILL.md §4 quality bar: &quot;passes the visual check&quot;","inspect-presentation.mjs header: &quot;Screenshots and report.json are inspection artifacts, not pass/fail evidence&quot;; it prints &quot;advisory warning(s)&quot;","Review guidance: &quot;fixing visual composition findings and re-inspecting satisfies the visual check&quot;; &quot;A pass/fail field in a completion report format is not a permission to complete wit…"],"citations":["skills/presentation/SKILL.md","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":1,"sample":2}],"verification-tooling":[],"engineering-quality":[{"id":"engineering-preview-readiness-bounded","classification":"contradicted","rationale":"The objection does not hold. The requirement says every wait for preview readiness must have a timeout. The wait in startPreview does: it sets a 30-second deadline (timeoutMs = 30000), checks it on every pass of the loop, and stops the preview and throws a Fail once it passes. The fetch inside the loop is one probe within that bounded wait, not a separate wait with no limit. A refused connection makes fetch fail at once and the loop retries every 150 ms. The objection only bites if vite preview accepted a connection and then never replied. Nothing in the material shows that happening, and the review guidance does not name that scenario, so it is a hypothetical input that cannot fail the criterion. Node&#39;s built-in fetch also gives up on its own after its default connect and header timeouts, so even that case would end. The objection itself accepts that the build-before-preview clause is met (both verifiers await runBuild before startPreview) and that the URL-parsing clause does not apply, because readiness is an HTTP probe rather than parsing printed output. All three clauses are met, so the pass stands.","evidence":["Both copies of scripts/lib/preview.mjs: `const deadline = Date.now() + timeoutMs` with `timeoutMs = 30000`; each loop pass runs `if (Date.now() &gt; deadline) { await stop(); throw new Fail(&#39;prev…","Readiness is `await fetch(`${url}/`)` inside try/catch. A refused connection throws at once and the loop retries after `setTimeout(resolve, 150)`. A fetch that hangs needs a server that accepts but n…","In both verify.mjs copies, `await runBuild(root)` completes and its exit code is checked before `startPreview(root)` is called. inspect-presentation.mjs does the same.","Readiness never reads the stdout or stderr log to find a ready URL. The log is only added to error messages, so the ANSI and split-chunk clause does not apply."],"citations":["scripts/lib/preview.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/lib/preview.mjs","scripts/verify.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/verify.mjs","scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs","skills/presentation/templates/bootstrap/scripts/inspect-presentation.mjs"],"marker":"","stage":"contradiction-check","panel_index":2,"sample":3}],"testing-evidence":[],"assumption-handling":[]}
